"""Persist and check the October 12 channel-check decision (read-only for workbook)."""
import json
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from openpyxl import load_workbook

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
d = json.loads((ROOT / 'analysis/2026-10-12-channel.json').read_text())
run_id = '8e4d912a97c74f539e96d685fece12f2'
stamp = '2026-10-12T13:53:37+00:00'

def verify_quotes(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        if 'source_id' in obj and 'quote' in obj:
            source = ROOT / 'sources' / (obj['source_id'] + '.txt')
            assert source.exists(), str(source)
            assert obj['quote'] in source.read_text(), str(obj)
        for item in obj.values():
            verify_quotes(item)
    elif isinstance(obj, list):
        for item in obj:
            verify_quotes(item)

verify_quotes(d)
w = load_workbook(ROOT / 'model/forecast.xlsx', data_only=False)
assert d['capex_changes'] == [] and len(d['changes']) == 1
assert d['changes'][0]['driver'] == 'nvda_share'
assert d['changes'][0]['scenario'] == 'bull' and d['changes'][0]['value'] == 0.655
expected = {
    'C4':150, 'C5':180, 'C6':137.5, 'C7':215,
    'B11':0.37, 'C11':0.38, 'D11':0.39,
    'B12':0.64, 'C12':0.65, 'D12':0.655,
    'B13':0.025, 'C13':0.027, 'D13':0.03,
    'B14':0.46, 'C14':0.45, 'D14':0.445,
    'B15':0.55, 'C15':0.5, 'D15':0.45}
for cell, value in expected.items():
    assert w['Inputs'][cell].value == value, (cell, w['Inputs'][cell].value, value)
quarters = {'B7':62.314, 'C7':75.246, 'D7':89.023, 'E7':103, 'B15':128}
for cell, value in quarters.items():
    assert w['Quarters'][cell].value == value
for cell, source in [('B10','nvda-2026-02-25-cfo'),('C10','nvda-2026-05-20-cfo'),('D10','nvda-2026-08-26-cfo')]:
    assert w['Quarters'][cell].value == source
assert w['Quarters']['F7'].value.startswith('=')
assert w['Model']['C4'].value.startswith('=')
assert 120 <= len(d['note'].split()) <= 250 and len(d['stance'].split()) <= 25
capex = sum(expected[f'C{i}'] for i in range(4,8))
known = 62.314/3 + 75.246 + 89.023
base = capex*0.38*0.65/0.45
old_bull = capex*0.39*0.66/0.445
new_bull = capex*0.39*0.655/0.445
base_q4 = (base-known-103)*1.5
bull_q4 = (new_bull-known-108)*1.5
result = {
    'capex_bn':capex, 'NVDA_base_bn':base, 'AMD_base_bn':capex*0.38*0.027/0.5,
    'NVDA_previous_bull_bn':old_bull, 'NVDA_new_bull_bn':new_bull,
    'bull_change_bn':new_bull-old_bull, 'bull_change_pct':(new_bull/old_bull-1)*100,
    'base_q4_required_bn':base_q4, 'conditional_bull_q3_bn':108,
    'conditional_bull_q4_required_bn':bull_q4, 'bull_q4_growth_pct':(bull_q4/108-1)*100,
    'conditional_new_order_earliest':str(date(2026,10,1)+timedelta(weeks=20)),
    'conditional_new_order_latest':str(date(2026,10,8)+timedelta(weeks=30)),
    'timing_is_arithmetic_not_disclosed_schedule':True}
(ROOT/'analysis/2026-10-12-channel-sensitivity.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')

# Preserve all existing capex/driver evidence and the on-record next-quarter forecast.
p = ROOT/'notes/thesis.md'
t = p.read_text()
t = t.replace('**Stance:** Capex tracks modestly above the street; NVIDIA benefits, while undisclosed GPU revenue keeps AMD’s base near consensus.',
              '**Stance:** '+d['stance'])
t = t.replace('Research as of 2026-10-12T13:40:23+00:00.', 'Research as of '+stamp+'.')
t = t.replace('The NVIDIA gap moves from -$5.62bn to +$2.62bn; AMD from +$1.22bn to approximately zero.',
              'At initiation the NVIDIA gap moved from -$5.62bn to +$2.62bn and AMD from +$1.22bn to approximately zero; this check leaves both base gaps unchanged. NVIDIA bull is now $391.79bn versus $372bn street, down $2.99bn from $394.78bn.')
t = t.replace('| NVIDIA spend share | 64% / 65% / 66% |',
              '| NVIDIA spend share | 64% / 65% / 65.5% |')
t = t.replace('Bear 58→64 and bull 70→66 jointly repair the quarterly extremes.',
              'At initiation bear 58→64 and bull 70→66 jointly repaired the quarterly extremes. The October channel check now halves the optional one-point bull premium: 66→65.5, a 0.5-point persistence-confidence haircut, not measured 2026 share loss [channel-oct2026].')
t = t.replace('| Bull | 394.78 / 17.75 | 108 / 152.60 | Stretch Q4 +41.3% needs substantial incremental Rubin conversion; not the base. |',
              '| Bull | 391.79 / approximately 17.745 | 108 / 148.12 | Stretch Q4 +37.1% needs substantial incremental Rubin conversion; not the base. AMD inputs unchanged. |')
section = """## October channel update

The October 1–8 synthetic interview report is a distinct document family from the company releases. All three ODM/OEM respondents describe larger 2027 cloud rack orders; two respondents describe rising custom-accelerator order share at two unnamed clouds; one planner says power availability sets 2027 deployment pace; neocloud leads describe stable NVIDIA lead times around 20–30 weeks and improving AMD system availability [channel-oct2026].

Count one check, not eight independent corroborations. Identities, order overlap, purchase values and custom-share denominators are absent. The custom point concerns new rack orders in a predominantly 2027 discussion; its exact delivery year is unstated. AWS's February Trainium3 production, April landed-chip mix/OpenAI 2027 ramp and July multi-gigawatt commitments independently support custom adoption, but cannot identify or verify the two anonymous clouds [amzn-2026-02-05-release] [amzn-2026-04-29-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release]. Chip-unit share and Graviton/Trainium/Nitro business revenue are not accelerator dollar share. No earlier eligible channel check provides a comparable lead-time baseline.

The new observation reduces confidence in favorable end-year share persistence; half of the 1-point upside capture premium is removed, reducing NVIDIA bull by 2.9907bn (-0.76%). Base/bear shares, accelerator mix, concentration, all company capex and all AMD drivers are held. Most of this check's exposure is 2027; no 2026 guide or dated shipment slip warrants a base reduction.

Power could defer energized capacity without cancelling demand. Orders, supplier delivery/acceptance, customer capex payments and energization can differ. I partly disagree with the vendor's “share, not volume” opinion: commissioned volume may also be power-limited. One planner is not evidence of a universal constraint or a specified company's delay. Stable lead times are not deterioration; conditionally, new October 1–8 orders at 20–30 weeks imply February 18–May 6, 2027, not a disclosed delivery schedule. Hold Q3 DC 103 and own Q4 128 until actual guide/delivery evidence changes their odds.

Next: identify primary company power-ready dates and supplier acceptance schedules ahead of late-October results/2027 guidance. A Microsoft FY26 annual-report IR fetch returned 404; company-specific power timing remains unresolved.

"""
if '## October channel update' not in t:
    t = t.replace('## Catalysts and disconfirmation\n', section+'## Catalysts and disconfirmation\n')
t = t.replace('- Late October 2026: hyperscaler Q3 cash capex, server/building mix and revised 2026/first 2027 guidance.',
              '- Late October 2026: hyperscaler Q3 cash capex, server/custom/building mix, power-ready dates and revised 2026/first 2027 guidance.\n- Before November results: comparable channel interviews with respondent-overlap methodology, custom-share units/dollars and actual delivery dates.')
position = """## Position thesis read

Latest check: NVIDIA long's upside capture leg weakens slightly, while larger forward orders support demand persistence. Base stays +2.62bn (+0.70%) versus street; bull gap narrows +22.78→+19.79bn. The overall base still supports the long, so this is not a new contrary base call or a >5% move. AMD base gap stays approximately zero; availability is not recognized GPU revenue.

The initiation evidence for MSFT demand/conversion remains; anonymous power/custom observations cannot be assigned to Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta or Amazon. Alphabet's TPU unit-cost premise remains unverified. Meta capex stays at street. Previously recorded AMD deployment-delay and Amazon margin-compression short questions remain open; this check adds no named shipment value or current margin disclosure [channel-oct2026] [amd-2026-08-04-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release].

No analyst guidance or settled decision has changed. No new attention item is warranted: base does not cross street, the only forecast movement is a 0.76% bull reduction, and verification remains a public-research question. Position decisions remain with the analyst and PM.
"""
t = t.split('## Position thesis read')[0] + position
p.write_text(t)

questions = '# Open questions — October 12, 2026, channel update\n\n'
questions += '\n\n'.join(f'{i}. {question}' for i,question in enumerate(d['open_questions'],1))
questions += '\n\nNext independent research: '+d['follow_up']+'\n'
questions += '\nPrior unresolved capex, concentration, NVIDIA actuals and AMD GPU questions remain carried forward. Independence, custom dollar share and a dated power-related slip are not established by this check.\n'
(ROOT/'notes/open-questions.md').write_text(questions)

entry = f"""## {stamp} — {d['headline']}

Run: {run_id}. Item: channel-oct2026, synthetic material channel check.

{d['note']}

Investigation: {d['investigation']['question']} Status: partially answered.

Finding: {d['investigation']['finding']}

What arrived: Supply Chain Signals' October 1–8 eight-person sample. Three ODM/OEM managers report larger 2027 rack orders; two unspecified respondents report rising custom share at two unnamed Big Four clouds; one planner identifies power as the 2027 pacing constraint; neocloud procurement leads report stable NVIDIA 20–30 week lead times and improving AMD rack availability. These are vendor-reported observations, not verified customer disclosures [channel-oct2026].

What I checked: Earlier eligible channel reports were absent in the source list/search. Compared with Amazon February Trainium3 production and Trainium4 2027 timing, April chip-count mix/OpenAI 2027 Trainium ramp, July multi-gigawatt commitments, NVIDIA August Rubin deployments and Q3 total guide, and AMD August Azure Helios/mixed CPU-GPU revenue. AWS primary disclosures support direction independently but do not validate the anonymous clouds, dollars or respondents. Chip counts and the broader CPU/custom-chip revenue business are not accelerator spending share. Date-filtered searches were used for prior disclosures; a separate unfiltered search included live-labelled channel documents. Microsoft annual-report URL https://www.microsoft.com/investor/reports/ar26/index.html returned 404, leaving operational power timing unresolved.

Demand versus timing: Larger orders support 2027 demand intentions, without quantified dollars or delivery dates. A power constraint can stage energization despite intact orders. The vendor's “share, not volume” opinion overlooks commissioned capacity. Stable lead times do not demonstrate new delay. Conditional October 1–8 new orders plus 20–30 weeks give February 18–May 6, 2027; this is illustrative arithmetic, not a procurement forecast or proof of customer acceptance timing.

Changed: Only Inputs!D12, NVIDIA bull spend share 66%→65.5%. Half the optional 1-point premium over 65% base is removed as judgment under forward, anonymous evidence. NVIDIA bull 394.7764→391.7857 (-2.9907, -0.76%); its street gap 22.78→19.79. At conditional bull Q3 108, required Q4 is now 148.118 (+37.1%), versus 152.604 previously. Base 374.6167, required base Q4 129.8645, own Q4 128, recorded Q3 103, capex 682.5 and all AMD inputs remain held. No inference of a measured 2026 share loss, a guide change or an established 2026 slip.

Verification: update_model records the single input change. analysis/channel_update.py validates every exact contiguous decision quote, all changed/held input cells, preserved reported quarter sources and output formulas. analysis/2026-10-12-channel-sensitivity.json records before/after mathematics and the conditional lead-time window. No output formula was overwritten.

Open: Respondent independence/order overlap; anonymous customer identity and custom units-versus-dollar share; specific power-ready/acceptance/deployment dates; comparable prior lead-time baseline. Existing capex, concentration, NVIDIA actuals, AMD GPU and 2027 guide questions are carried forward in notes/open-questions.md.

Next: {d['follow_up']}

Attention: none. Base remains above street; the only forecast move is a 0.76% bull reduction. The report weakens the upside capture leg without making the overall NVIDIA base contrary to the held long. Previously recorded AMD/Amazon position-premise questions are not re-escalated on anonymous availability alone.

Position read: NVIDIA long's capture thesis weakens slightly in the upside; base street gap stays +2.62 (+0.70%), bull gap narrows +22.78→+19.79. AMD base gap stays approximately zero; no recognized GPU dollars were added.
"""
log = ROOT/'notes/research-log.md'
old = log.read_text()
if run_id not in old:
    log.write_text(old.rstrip()+'\n\n'+entry)
for name in ['research-log.md','open-questions.md','thesis.md']:
    assert '[channel-oct2026]' in (ROOT/'notes'/name).read_text() or name == 'open-questions.md'
assert '65.5%' in (ROOT/'notes/thesis.md').read_text()
assert '391.79' in (ROOT/'notes/thesis.md').read_text()
for question in d['open_questions']:
    assert question in (ROOT/'notes/open-questions.md').read_text()
print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
print('Exact quotes, input agreement, quarter sources, formulas and persistent notes verified.')
